title: Crestline Paid Upgrade Price List and Upgrade Eligibility
content:
**Price list — cabin upgrades on Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** Prices are per segment in US dollars. A short segment is 1000 statute miles or less; a long segment is longer than 1000 miles (the segment length threshold of the seat fee schedule, the same 1000 miles on every brand).

| Fare brand | Complimentary Summit upgrade or upgrade certificate may clear | Paid upgrade sold | Upgrade into Premium Economy | Upgrade into First, short segment | Upgrade into First, long segment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crestline Basic Economy | No | No | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Crestline Main Cabin | Yes | Yes | 99 | 149 | 329 |
| Crestline Main Plus | Yes | Yes | 79 | 129 | 299 |
| Crestline Main Flexible | Yes | Yes | 99 | 149 | 329 |
| Crestline Premium Economy | Yes | Yes | 0 | 99 | 229 |
| Crestline First | No | No | 0 | 0 | 0 |

## Notes to the price list

- A price of 0 marks an upgrade that is not sold on that brand: Crestline Basic Economy and Crestline First sell no paid upgrade, and a Crestline Premium Economy ticket is already in the Premium Economy cabin.
- The first column records whether the fare brand may clear a complimentary Summit elite upgrade or an upgrade certificate.
- *Hypothetical reading:* on a Crestline Main Plus ticket, an upgrade into First on a 1,000-mile segment is listed at 129 dollars and on a 1,300-mile segment at 299 dollars; an upgrade into Premium Economy is listed at 79 dollars whatever the segment length.
